title: Gain Path
similar: LeetCode 124 Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
hints: A best path has a highest node (closest to the root). Imagine you fix that node: what two things hang off it?
Each side is a downward chain that starts at a child. Define down[v] = the best sum of a chain that starts at v and only goes downward. A side that would make the total smaller can simply be skipped.

down[v] = gain[v] + max(0, down[left], down[right]); the best path through v is gain[v] + max(0, down[left]) + max(0, down[right]); answer = the maximum over all v. Children have larger indices than their parent, so a loop from n-1 down to 0 visits children first and needs no recursion.

wrong.root_to_leaf.cpp: only considers paths that start at the root
wrong.no_clamp.cpp: adds a child's chain even when it is negative
wrong.tle_rewalk.cpp: re-walks the whole subtree below every node (fails the perf group)

strategy.question: Scout the statement: a tree of up to 2*10^5 nodes with signed gains, find the best connected path (it may bend at one node and need not touch the root). Which plan fits?
options: Try every pair of nodes and sum the path between them
One bottom-up pass: for each node, combine its two best downward chains (skipping negative ones) and keep a running maximum
Sort nodes by gain and add the largest ones that stay connected
Take the root and follow the larger child at every step
strategy.why: Pairs of nodes cost O(n^2) pairs times a path walk. Sorting by gain ignores that the chosen nodes must form a path. Following the larger child misses paths that bend and paths that avoid the root. A bottom-up pass computes down[v] once per node, so the whole tree costs O(n).
